clue.text: Advantage for the pound? Always, given time!

blocks.note: L is the symbol for a pound sterling, from the Latin libra
a synonym meaning at all times
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A cheerleader for sterling argues it always gains an edge if you just wait long enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the pound' looks like the currency being discussed; it supplies only the single-letter symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: Leverage is the power or edge that lets someone gain something, so it serves as a synonym.

clue.text: Call is diverted through bloomers

indicators.note: something diverted is sent off a different route, so the letters change course

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A phone call rerouted through someone's underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomers' suggests old-fashioned knickers; here it means things that bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: Lilacs are flowering shrubs, so in crossword fashion they are bloomers, things that produce blossoms.

clue.text: Sell gold in the cellar, reportedly

definitions.note: 'cellar, reportedly' is a sound-alike for seller

blocks.note: to vend is to sell
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: Selling off gold kept down in the basement, so it is said.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' applies to the definition: 'cellar' said aloud is seller.
explanation.definitionFit: A vendor is a person who offers goods for money, which is a seller, the word cellar sounds like.

clue.text: Fight for another chance at exam around start of September

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, which is all that is kept
around means encircling, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: a resit is a second attempt at an examination
the initial letter of the month

explanation.surface: A student pushing for a retake of an exam at the start of autumn term.
explanation.walkthrough: A resit is the British term for retaking a failed exam.
explanation.definitionFit: To resist is to oppose or struggle against something, so it is a synonym of fight as a verb.

clue.text: Fruit for the third person

blocks.note: first meaning: a tart green berry
second meaning: an unwanted extra person accompanying a couple

explanation.walkthrough: 'the third person' sounds like grammar (he, she, it); it is the British idiom for being an unwanted third wheel to a couple.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a sour berry, and to play it is British slang for the awkward extra tagging along with lovers.

clue.text: Maniac chops your head off!

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept
off suggests something gone wrong or out of kilter, so the letters are put in a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
the initial letter of the word your

explanation.surface: A horror-film warning that the madman will decapitate you.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'head off' as decapitation; actually 'head' takes the first letter of 'your' and 'off' scrambles it with CHOPS to give PSYCHO.
explanation.definitionFit: Psycho is informal slang for a dangerously unstable, crazed person, which is what a maniac is.

clue.text: Sensible case for brewing true wine

indicators.note: a case holds something inside it, so the first piece surrounds the second
brewing mixes ingredients together, so the letters are stirred into a new order

blocks.note: sane means sensible or rational
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sensible argument for making genuine wine at home.
explanation.definitionFit: Sauterne is a sweet white dessert wine from the Sauternes district of Bordeaux.

clue.text: Belief in alternative new creed within the Church

indicators.note: an alternative version is a different form, so the letters take another order

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for new
taken as written
CE stands for the Church of England

explanation.surface: Faith in a different, newly devised creed inside the Church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'within' is loose: the scrambled letters simply come before CE rather than inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Credence is acceptance that something is true, so giving credence means having faith or belief in it.

clue.text: Try alone to produce in an ostentatious way

indicators.note: producing something means making it from raw materials, so these letters are remade

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Advice to attempt something solo in order to make a showy result.
explanation.definitionFit: Done ornately means elaborately decorated and showy, which is ostentatious.

clue.text: Cricketer yearns for a spinner

blocks.note: to long for something is to yearn for it
a spinning top is a toy that spins

explanation.surface: A cricketer pining for a slow bowler to come on.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a spinner is a slow bowler, which is the false path; here it is the toy. A long stop is a fielder placed directly behind the wicketkeeper.
explanation.definitionFit: Long stop names a fielding position in cricket and the player standing there, so the fielder is a cricketer.

clue.text: Very dirty stables cleaned for what sounds like an orgy on reflection

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror shows things the other way round, so the two words swap order
the answer is identified by how it is spoken rather than how it is spelt

blocks.note: the two words read in the opposite order, then said out loud

explanation.surface: Filthy stables scrubbed out, and the scene described as a debauched party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on reflection' swaps the two words, giving 'orgy an', which said out loud is the answer. The stables are a reference: Hercules cleaned the filthy stables of King Augeas.
explanation.definitionFit: Augean means extremely filthy or neglected, from the stables of Augeas that went uncleaned for thirty years.

clue.text: Leading Catholic to hang around about second walkway

indicators.note: leading here means placed at the front, before the remaining letters
about means surrounding, so one piece goes around the other

blocks.note: C is a standard abbreviation for Catholic
to loiter is to linger or hang around
S is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: A senior Catholic is invited to linger near a corridor.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloister is a covered walkway, usually around a quadrangle in a monastery or cathedral.

clue.text: Centre redesigned not long ago

definitions.note: an adverbial phrase for an adjective; read as 'of not long ago'

indicators.note: something redesigned has its parts rearranged into a new form

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A town centre that was given a makeover only lately.
explanation.definitionFit: Something recent happened or appeared a short while back, in the near past.

clue.text: One improving retail outlet finds second step more suitable

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second
a hop is a little step or jump
fitter is the comparative of fit, meaning suitable

explanation.surface: A shop refurbisher decides the next stage of a plan suits better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second step' looks like one phrase; S and HOP are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A shopfitter is a tradesperson who installs counters, shelving and fixtures inside stores, upgrading the premises.

clue.text: Machine out of order: airman returns, acting without any thought

indicators.note: a machine out of order is broken, so its letters are jumbled
returning means going back, so the word is read from end to start

blocks.note: taken as written
LAC stands for leading aircraftman, a junior RAF rank

explanation.surface: A broken machine, and an airman doing his job on autopilot.
explanation.walkthrough: LAC, leading aircraftman, is a rank in Britain's Royal Air Force.
explanation.definitionFit: Mechanical describes behaviour done automatically, by rote or habit, like a machine without conscious reflection.

clue.text: Type of group that could get under one's skin

definitions.text: that could get under one's skin

blocks.note: first meaning: a breakaway faction

blocks.clueFragment: that could get under one's skin
blocks.note: second meaning: a sliver of wood lodged in flesh

explanation.walkthrough: 'get under one's skin' reads as the idiom for annoyance; here it is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: A splinter group breaks off from a party, and a splinter is a thin shard of wood that pierces the skin.

clue.text: Housing charming creature in a filthy setting shows harshness

indicators.note: housing something means giving it a home inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: taken as written
a sty is a pigpen, a famously dirty place
a peri is a beautiful fairy of Persian legend

explanation.surface: A fairy kept in a grimy dwelling reveals a rough side.
explanation.walkthrough: A peri is a creature from Persian myth; a sty, the pigpen, is the filthy setting that houses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Asperity is roughness or severity of tone or manner, a formal synonym for harshness.

clue.text: Shock that sin has to out

indicators.note: out suggests something disordered or wrong, so the letters go into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Outrage that a misdeed must be exposed publicly.
explanation.definitionFit: To astonish someone is to amaze or stun them, which is shocking them as a verb.

clue.text: Send text consisting of later thoughts

definitions.note: plural in the clue; the answer is one such afterthought

blocks.note: to post a letter is to send it
a script is a written text

explanation.surface: Instructions to send a message containing some afterthoughts.
explanation.definitionFit: A postscript is an extra note added at the end of a letter, holding afterthoughts written after signing.

clue.text: A doctor with English degree on primitive life form

blocks.note: taken as written
MO is a medical officer, an army doctor
E is the abbreviation for English
a BA is a Bachelor of Arts degree

explanation.surface: A doctor holding an English degree studying early organisms.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'on' puts the degree below the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: An amoeba is a single-celled organism, a simple and ancient kind of living thing.

clue.text: Way to irritate a pain in the side

blocks.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
to itch is to cause irritation

explanation.surface: A way of annoying someone who is already a pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a pain in the side' echoes the idiom 'thorn in the side'; here it is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: A stitch is a sharp cramp felt under the ribs, typically when running.

clue.text: Merchant about to move quickly up

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means reading the letters from bottom to top

blocks.note: re means about or concerning
to dart is to dash

explanation.surface: A merchant about to hurry upstairs.
explanation.definitionFit: A trader buys and sells goods for profit, which is what a merchant does.

clue.text: Pack chest for a cold place

blocks.note: pack ice is the floating ice of polar seas, so pack suggests ice
a chest is a large box

explanation.surface: Packing a trunk for a trip somewhere freezing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pack' looks like the verb for filling a case; it is the noun, as in pack ice.
explanation.definitionFit: An icebox is a cooled cabinet or refrigerator, a chilly spot; it is also slang for a freezing location.

clue.text: Tame ride around the Central Line

indicators.note: around suggests letters spun about and scattered into a fresh sequence

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A gentle trip on London's Central Line Underground route.
explanation.walkthrough: The Central Line is a London Underground line, which is the misdirection; here it is a line through the centre of a circle.
explanation.definitionFit: A diameter is the straight chord passing through the middle of a circle, joining two opposite points.

clue.text: Unimportant details about time Queen's leaving Riviera

indicators.note: leaving means departing, so those letters go out of the word

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time
taken as written
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword Queen

explanation.surface: Gossip about when the Queen is departing the French Riviera.
explanation.definitionFit: Trivia are trifling facts or matters of little significance.

clue.text: Gave evidence on wrong date to hold trial

indicators.note: something wrong is not right, so the letters are set in another order
to hold something is to keep it inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: taken as written
a test is a trial

explanation.surface: A witness testified to the wrong date in court.
explanation.walkthrough: The scrambled date splits in two so the trial can sit in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: To attest is to bear witness or certify that something is true, so attested means testified.

clue.text: Poor Mr Hythe, having no energy, got beat

indicators.note: having none of something means it has been removed from the name
poor suggests being in a bad way, so the letters are knocked into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: An exhausted Mr Hythe, with no energy left, was given a beating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beat' looks like the past tense of a beating; it is the noun, a musical pulse.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhythm is the regular pulse or pattern of stresses in music, which is what a beat is.

clue.text: Break a nose

blocks.note: first meaning: a short rest or pause
second meaning, whimsically: something that does the breathing

explanation.walkthrough: 'Break a nose' reads as an injury; the two halves are separate meanings, the second a playful literal one.
explanation.definitionFit: A short pause to rest is a breather, and a nose, which draws in air, is jokingly one that breathes.
